title: Why Are Tunnel Boring Machines Left Underground?
description:
Under the sea between England and France, there is a machine that will never see daylight again. It dug part of the Channel Tunnel, and when the job was done, the workers did not bring it back. They steered it down into the rock, out of the way, and left it there. Today, eleven parts of a tunnel boring machine, and why each one exists, starting with the strange reason so many of them stay underground.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 11 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:11 1. The machine left in the ground
2:36 2. The steel discs on the cutterhead
3:52 3. The concrete puzzle pieces
5:04 4. The jacks that push off the walls
6:22 5. The grout behind the ring
7:29 6. The chamber full of mud
8:51 7. The train behind the machine
9:55 8. The seals that failed under Seattle
11:05 9. The name on every machine
12:13 10. The laser that steers
13:27 11. The longest tunnel's machines
14:37 The verdict

Sources:
- Tunnel boring machines (shields, disc cutters, segment erectors, thrust jacks, grippers, EPB and slurry shields, backup): Wikipedia, "Tunnel boring machine" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_boring_machine ; Herrenknecht product pages https://www.herrenknecht.com/
- Channel Tunnel (buried British TBMs, breakthrough 1 December 1990, alignment error ~358 mm / 58 mm, TBM sold online 2004): Wikipedia, "Channel Tunnel" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_Tunnel ; BBC News, "Channel tunnel machine sold on eBay" (2004) http://news.bbc.co.uk/
- Tail void grouting, settlement monitoring and compensation grouting on Crossrail: Crossrail Learning Legacy https://learninglegacy.crossrail.co.uk/
- Crossrail TBM names (eight machines named after women): Crossrail https://www.crossrail.co.uk/
- Bertha / SR 99 tunnel (17.5 m, stopped Dec 2013, rescue pit, resumed Dec 2015, breakthrough April 2017, opened Feb 2019): Wikipedia, "Bertha (tunnel boring machine)" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertha_(tunnel_boring_machine) ; WSDOT https://wsdot.wa.gov/
- Saint Barbara, patron saint of miners and tunnellers: Wikipedia, "Saint Barbara" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barbara
- Gotthard Base Tunnel (57 km, opened 2016, 2,300 m overburden, rock temperature up to ~46 °C, four gripper TBMs, construction 1999-2016): Wikipedia, "Gotthard Base Tunnel" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotthard_Base_Tunnel ; AlpTransit Gotthard AG
- TBM guidance (laser total station and target): VMT GmbH, "TBM guidance systems" https://www.vmt-gmbh.de/
